{{Top|canon=Activator (lightsaber component)}}
[[File:LumiyasLightwhipHilt-SW1977-96.jpg|thumb|right|300px|[[Lumiya]] presses the activation stud on [[Lumiya's lightwhip|her lightwhip]].]]
{{Quote|How does it work?''"<br />"''On the same principle as my whip&hellip;when you activate that stud on the hilt, it releases a beam of coherent energy which forms the sword blade.|[[Den Siva]] and Lumiya|<ref name="Star Wars (1977) 96">[[Star Wars (1977) 96|''Star Wars'' (1977) 96]]</ref>}}
The '''activation stud''', '''button''', '''slide''', '''switch''', '''lever''', or '''plate''', was a component on the [[Lightsaber hilt/Legends|hilt]] of a [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]] or [[Lightwhip/Legends|lightwhip]] that activated the weapon's energy blade. It was generally a prominent button, although [[Asajj Ventress/Legends|Asajj Ventress]] concealed the activation switches on [[Asajj Ventress's lightsabers/Legends|her lightsabers]].<ref name="New Essential Guide to Weapons and Technology">''[[The New Essential Guide to Weapons and Technology]]''</ref>

When a lightsaber was activated, it stayed active until the wielder pressed the activation button again to deactivate it. However, if the lightsaber had a [[pressure grip]], it automatically deactivated when the wielder was no longer holding the lightsaber, such as when the wielder was disarmed. A lightsaber could also have a [[locking activator]], which was a specialized activation stud that could lock the lightsaber's blade into the activated position, even when the wielder was not holding the lightsaber. This allowed the wielder to use the lightsaber as a [[Telekinesis/Legends|thrown]] weapon. Locking the blade prevented it from being accidentally deactivated when the weapon impacted the target.<ref name="Jedi Academy Training Manual">''[[Jedi Academy Training Manual]]''</ref>

[[File:Lightsaber_hilt_schematics_NEGWT.jpg|thumb|left|300px|A lightsaber hilt showing an activation plate]]
A [[trapped grip]] was another modification that was used to prevent unauthorized users from activating the lightsaber. If someone attempted to activate it without disarming the trap, they would be injured by an energy discharge.<ref name="Jedi Academy Training Manual" />

A rare modification was the [[Force-activated]] lightsaber. This required the wielder to activate their lightsaber using the Force, thus removing the activation button from the lightsaber's hilt.<ref name="Jedi Academy Training Manual" />

Skillful activation and deactivation of a lightsaber was a key feature in [[Tràkata/Legends|Tràkata]], a form of [[Lightsaber combat/Legends|lightsaber combat]] that involved repeatedly activating and deactivating the lightsaber. For example, a technique called "Pass the blade" was used to deactivate the lightsaber then reactivate it to pass through an opponent's block.<ref name="Jedi Academy Training Manual" />

Lightsabers had other buttons and knobs that adjusted the blade's length and its power or intensity.<ref name="Star Wars: The Visual Dictionary">''[[Star Wars: The Visual Dictionary]]''</ref> In a [[Dual-phase lightsaber/Legends|dual-phase lightsaber]], a second lightsaber blade could be activated that was twice the length of a normal blade.<ref name="Jedi Academy Training Manual" />

[[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] [[Lorana Jinzler]]'s [[Lorana Jinzler's lightsaber|lightsaber]] had an [[Amethyst/Legends|amethyst]] attached to its activation stud.<ref name="Outbound Flight">[[Outbound Flight (novel)|''Outbound Flight'']]</ref>
